slides.title: What is an Interface?
slides.content: An interface defines a contract: a set of members that implementing classes must provide. It contains only declarations, no implementation.
slides.exampleOutput: Interface definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: Declaring an Interface
slides.content: Use the 'interface' keyword. By convention, interface names start with 'I'. Members are implicitly public and abstract.
slides.exampleOutput: Interface definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: Implementing an Interface
slides.content: A class uses a colon to implement an interface and must provide implementations for all interface members.
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition with a method that writes to the console; produces no output unless the method is invoked.

exercise.prompt: Complete the class declaration to implement the interface.

slides.title: Multiple Interfaces
slides.content: A class can implement multiple interfaces separated by commas. This enables flexible composition of behaviors.
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: Interface Properties and Events
slides.content: Interfaces can declare properties and events. Implementing classes must implement these members.
slides.exampleOutput: Interface definition; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Which members can an interface declare?

slides.title: Interface vs Abstract Class
slides.content: Use interfaces for contracts across unrelated types. Use abstract classes for shared base behavior in a class hierarchy.

slides.title: Explicit Interface Implementation
slides.content: A class can explicitly implement an interface member, hiding it from the public API and requiring casting to access.
slides.exampleOutput: Interface definition with a method that writes to the console; produces no output unless the method is invoked.

slides.title: Interface Best Practices
slides.content: Keep interfaces small and focused (Interface Segregation Principle). Name them clearly with the 'I' prefix. Prefer interfaces for dependency injection.
